title: How do we find these sums and differences?
description: Six sums and differences with tenths and hundredths are found by adding place by place with carrying and by taking away with breaking. The last difference is checked by adding back.
teaching_notes: One idea: add place by place and carry when a place fills, take away place by place and break when a place is too small. Watch for children who forget that three tenths is thirty hundredths.

source: Figure it Out (hundredths), the set of six sums and differences
video_script.why: The child has added with carrying and taken away with breaking, and now does both on six new numbers.
video_script.substitution: Add place by place and carry when a place fills; take away place by place and break from the next place when a place is too small.
video_script.anchor: Six sums and differences written in columns of units, tenths and hundredths
video_script.payoff_line: Carry when a place fills, and break when a place is too small

final_answer.spoken: three and thirty four hundredths, eleven and seven tenths, thirty, three and three hundredths twice, and eleven and sixty three hundredths

maths_rules: 9 5/10 7/100 + 2 1/10 3/100: units 11, tenths 6 + 1 = 7, hundredths 7 + 3 = 10 = 1 tenth, so tenths 7 and hundredths 0: 11 7/10.
15 6/10 4/100 + 14 3/10 6/100: units 29, tenths 9, hundredths 10 carries 1 tenth, tenths 10 carries 1 unit: 30.
video_script.design: The six sums stay in the anchor band; each is worked by place in the working band, and the last difference is checked by adding back. The method is the carrying and breaking of the solved sums.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; six sums and differences with tenths and hundredths written in a list

marks.book: the title card arrives: From your book
marks.six: six sums and differences are written in a list
marks.ask: a question mark appears beside the list

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Six sums and differences are written with tenths and hundredths.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can we find each one the way we did before?

beats.on_screen: the six sums stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: ten hundredth blocks join into one tenth; one tenth block breaks into ten hundredth blocks

marks.add: ten hundredth blocks join into one tenth block
marks.sub: one tenth block breaks into ten hundredth blocks

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>To add, work place by place and carry when a place holds ten.
<bookmark mark='sub'/>To take away, break one from the next bigger place when a place has too few.

marks.given: the six sums and differences are written one under the other

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, three sums and three differences, all written on the board.

beats.on_screen: To find: the value of each one

marks.find: the words the value of each one are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the value of each one.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, the first sum. Three tenths is thirty hundredths.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Thirty hundredths and four hundredths make thirty four hundredths, with three units.

beats.on_screen: Sum 2: units 11, tenths 6 + 1 = 7, hundredths 7 + 3 = 10 = 1 tenth. Sum 3: units 29, tenths 9, hundredths 4 + 6 = 10 carries 1 tenth, tenths 10 carries 1 unit

marks.two: Sum 2 is added place by place and the hundredths 10 carry 1 tenth
marks.three: in Sum 3 the hundredths carry 1 tenth and the tenths carry 1 unit

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, the next two sums need carrying. In the second, the hundredths make ten, which is one tenth, so the tenths become seven.
<bookmark mark='three'/>In the third, the hundredths carry a tenth, and then ten tenths carry a unit, giving thirty.

beats.on_screen: Take away 1: hundredths 3, tenths 0, units 3. Take away 2: hundredths 3, units 3

marks.four: 7 7/100 - 4 4/100 leaves 3 hundredths, no tenths and 3 units

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step three, the next two need no breaking. In the first, seven take away four leaves three hundredths and three units.
<bookmark mark='five'/>The second works the same way, and leaves the same.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Step four, the last difference needs breaking. There are two hundredths and nine to take away, so break one tenth.
<bookmark mark='break'/>Then five tenths is less than nine, so break one unit.
<bookmark mark='res'/>The hundredths leave three, the tenths leave six, and the units are eleven.

marks.back: the total 12 62/100 is matched with the number we started with

narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Step five, check the last difference by adding back what we took away. Sixty three and ninety nine make one hundred sixty two hundredths.
<bookmark mark='back'/>That makes twelve and sixty two hundredths, which is the number we started with.

marks.ans: the six answers are written in order and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Carry when a place fills, and break when a place is too small.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The answers are three and thirty four hundredths, eleven and seven tenths, and thirty.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Then three and three hundredths twice, and eleven and sixty three hundredths.
